newsitem.title: UK: FDA panel recommends Rhone-Poulenc heart drug.
newsitem.headline: FDA panel recommends Rhone-Poulenc heart drug.

text.p: Rhone-Poulenc Rorer Inc said a U.S. Food and Drugs Administration panel had recommended approval of its heart drug Lovenox (enoxaparin sodium).
It said the Cardiovascular and Renal Drugs Advisory Committee had recommended approval of Lovenox injection for unstable angina and heart attack.

"The committee reviewed results of a multicentre international clinical trial known as the ESSENCE trial which showed Lovenox to be more effective than unfractionated intravenous heparin -- the current standard of care for unstable angina -- in reducing the combined endpoint of death, heart attack, or recurrent chest pain," the company said in a statement released in London.
Rhone-Poulenc is majority owned by French chemicals group Rhone-Poulenc SA. Unstable angina is severe chest pain, caused by a decrease in blood and oxygen to the heart muscle.
Patients are usually hospitalised as it often precedes heart attacks.

"Successfully treating the unstable angina patient is a critical first step in preventing a heart attack in that patient," Dr Marc Cohen of Allegheny University in Philadelphia said in the statement. -- London Newsroom 44-171-542-8958
